analyst_view.overall: Early view: Inter (15th, 6 points) have won three of their last four, including 3-0 at Feyenoord and 2-0 against Como on 8 November, with only a 3-1 derby defeat to Milan in between. Stuttgart (14th, 7 points) lost 2-0 at Galatasaray but beat Werder Bremen 1-0 at the weekend. Hakan Calhanoglu is listed as banned after his third yellow card; he was booked at Feyenoord, but I could not confirm the two earlier cautions, so that needs checking nearer the game.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.3 goals and I lean lower. Inter have kept clean sheets in three of their last four games (Venezia, Feyenoord, Como), and Stuttgart failed to score in Istanbul. Without Calhanoglu, Inter's build-up loses some of its quality, which points to a narrower game.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.1 corners. Inter will have more of the ball at San Siro and use their wing-backs, and Stuttgart are capable of pushing forward. I see nothing that moves the figure.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.9 cards and I lean slightly higher. Stuttgart had five players booked in Istanbul (Atakan Karazor, Deniz Undav, Yanik Spalt, Grischa Promel, Ramon Hendriks), and Inter had two booked at Feyenoord. A side that collected five bookings in its last away game in this competition is a fair pointer.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.2 shots and I lean lower. Calhanoglu is one of Inter's main shooters from distance, and his absence takes some volume away. Inter also tend to manage games once they lead.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.1 shots on target. Lautaro Martinez and Marcus Thuram will still create chances, and Ermedin Demirovic has four goals in four games for Stuttgart in this competition. I stay with the estimate.
